title: Ratio-based traffic scaler and quantile consistency prover for replay fidelity
author: Priya Desai
release_notes: Add a ratio-based traffic scaler to synthesize steady and burst phases from sampled traces
Introduce a quantile consistency prover metric suite and reporting pipeline (JSON + proto outputs)
Expose runtime knobs for seed drift and warmup epochs via --scale-ratio and --warmup-epochs
description: Motivation: The existing replay replayers produce plausible throughput profiles but struggle to preserve quantile structure when we rescale traffic for different cluster sizes or mixed tenancy. This PR introduces a ratio-based traffic scaler that refactors the replayer pipeline to (a) resample trace sessions proportionally to a user-specified ratio space, (b) preserve per-session relative timing using a lightweight stochastic time warp, and (c) emit a compact fingerprint for epochal warmup alignment. It also adds a Quantile Consistency Prover (QCP) that computes multi-epoch comparisons of p50/p95/p99 across replay runs and flags regressions above configurable tolerances. Changes: single PR implementing three coordinated pieces: 1) replay/scale: new scaler module that accepts --scale-ratio, --seed-drift, and --target-concurrency to produce deterministic scaled traces; supports both deterministic downsample and weighted-upsample with session jitter to avoid synthetic synchronization; 2) warmup-fingerprint: epochal fingerprinting that hashes sequence length & k-v cache hit estimates to align warmup checkpoints across heterogeneous runs; 3) qcp-reporter: a reporting pipeline stage that emits per-epoch quantile deltas, histogram serialized JSON and a small protobuf summary usable by dashboards. Compatibility: Designed to slot into existing benchmark-lab replay runner (no API changes to runner CLI other than optional flags). Backwards-compatible output formats (keeps old CSV summary alongside new JSON/proto). Implementation notes: - Adds a new scaler package under bench/replay/scaler with a small deterministic RNG shim to ensure reproducible upsampling. - Warmup fingerprinting uses xxhash64 and a compact proto schema bench/protos/warmup.proto. - QCP uses reservoir-sampled token stream to compute stable quantiles with streaming t-digest fallback for very large payloads. - Adds unit tests for edge cases: single-session bursts, symmetric upsample/downsample, and cache-priming empty traces. - Integrates new reporter into the CI pipeline and an e2e smoke job that runs a micro-replay and validates QCP thresholds. Checklist: - [x] Design doc attached in PR comments with sample outputs and dashboard mock - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration pipeline job - [x] Perf microbenchmark and baseline recording - [x] Docs snippet describing CLI flags and output formats Known limitations and follow-ups: - Upsampling retains relative ordering but can introduce synthetic inter-session dependencies; follow-up will add optional inter-session independence mode. - QCP currently uses fixed t-digest parameters; a future PR will expose adaptive parameterization. How this helps: provides a reproducible way to scale customer traces across capacity targets while preserving key tail properties; streamlines alerting by attaching a single QCP verdict to each run; enables per-commit regression detection in the dashboard.
commits: Initial scaler implementation and deterministic RNG shim
Warmup fingerprint proto + integration and tests
QCP reporter, dashboard payloads, and CI job
